title: Sequential Uniform Boundedness with Countable Choice

items.title: Two signs detect an operator increment
items.statement: Over either the real or complex scalar field, for every bounded linear operator T:X→Y between normed spaces and x,u∈X, max(||T(x+u)||,||T(x−u)||)≥||Tu||. No completeness or choice principle is assumed.
items.strategy: Linearity gives 2Tu=T(x+u)−T(x−u). The triangle inequality and absolute homogeneity give 2||Tu||≤||T(x+u)||+||T(x−u)||≤2 max(||T(x+u)||,||T(x−u)||). Divide by 2. This is Sokal equation (2), not a use of his local-ball lemma or family theorem. It actually holds for any linear T; boundedness matches the intended operator interface.

references.title: Sokal, A really simple elementary proof of the uniform boundedness theorem

items.title: Sequential uniform boundedness under countable choice
items.statement: Assume AC_omega over ZF. Let X be Banach and Y normed over the same field K=R or C. Let (T_k)_{k∈N}, N={0,1,...}, be a given sequence of bounded linear maps X→Y. If for every x∈X there is M_x<∞ with ||T_k x||≤M_x for all k, then there is M<∞ with ||T_k||≤M for all k. Completeness of Y, HB, DC and full AC are not hypotheses.
items.strategy: Argue by contradiction. The zero-domain case has all norms zero. For each auxiliary integer n≥1 define k_n=min{k∈N:||T_k||≥4^n}; unboundedness makes this set nonempty. The k_n need not be strictly increasing, and no subsequence assertion is used. Put S_n=T_{k_n}. From the unit-ball supremum and rescaling to the sphere, E_n={v∈X:||v||=1 and ||S_n v||>(2/3)||S_n||} is nonempty: otherwise (2/3)||S_n|| would bound the unit sphere and then the ball, contradicting ||S_n||>0. Apply AC_omega once to (E_{n+1})_{n∈N}, obtaining all v_n independently of all partial sums. Set x_0=0. For n≥1 set u_n=3^(−n)v_n and choose epsilon_n=+1 when ||S_n(x_{n−1}+u_n)||≥||S_n(x_{n−1}−u_n)||, and −1 otherwise; equality always takes +1. Define x_n=x_{n−1}+epsilon_n u_n. This is a total deterministic recursion on N×X, using state (n,x_n) and the already fixed vector sequence, so thm-recursion applies without DC. The preceding lemma gives ||S_n x_n||>(2/3)3^(−n)||S_n||. For m>n, the triangle inequality and the finite geometric identity give ||x_m−x_n||≤sum_{j=n+1}^m3^(−j)=(3^(−n)/2)(1−3^(−(m−n)))≤3^(−n)/2. Prove 3^n≥n+1 by induction and use thm-of-archimedean to see 3^(−n)→0. Thus the displayed x_n is Cauchy and the stated Banach hypothesis gives one limit x∈X. For fixed n, ||x−x_n||≤||x−x_m||+3^(−n)/2 for m>n; letting the first term tend to zero proves ||x−x_n||≤3^(−n)/2 without a separate continuity theorem. Operator-norm rescaling gives ||S_n(x−x_n)||≤||S_n||||x−x_n||. Hence ||S_n x||≥||S_n x_n||−||S_n||||x−x_n||>(1/6)3^(−n)||S_n||≥(1/6)(4/3)^n. Induction gives (4/3)^n≥1+n/3, so this contradicts M_x by the Archimedean property. The finite geometric identity follows by multiplying the finite sum by 3 and subtracting; no scalar-series theorem or series-to-Banach-completeness equivalence is imported. Label independent-vector selection and deterministic signs as the library adaptation of Sokal; neither Sokal nor the textbook is credited with this precise axiom audit.

references.title: Sokal, A really simple elementary proof of the uniform boundedness theorem
Lin and Rodriguez, MIT 18.102 Complete Lecture Notes
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis

title: Sequential Uniform Boundedness with Countable Choice: Examples

items.title: Coordinate partial sums on c_0
items.statement: For K=R or C and X=c_0(K) with the supremum norm, let e_j be the standard coordinate vector and P_Nx=sum_{j=0}^N x_j e_j. Then X is Banach, each P_N is a bounded linear operator X→X, P_Nx→x for every x∈X, and ||P_N||=1 for every N≥0. Under AC_omega the sequential theorem also gives the qualitative uniform bound; the displayed exact bound and convergence are choice-free.
items.strategy: Use def-c-zero-and-ell-infinity with zero-based coordinates. Supply Banach completeness locally, avoiding an edge to the B-page ex-c0-is-a-banach-space. The required least-upper-bound property of the library's real field is supplied by cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete, not by the bare definition def-complete-ordered-field: a real Cauchy sequence a_m is bounded (bound its tail within 1 of one term and bound the finitely many earlier terms); each tail has infimum b_N, and L=sup_N b_N exists. Given a Cauchy tail of diameter <eta, for any m on it every later tail infimum lies between a_m−eta and a_m+eta, and earlier tail infima are no larger than the current one. Thus |a_m−L|≤eta. Uniqueness follows from the triangle inequality. For complex scalars apply this to real and imaginary parts; |Re z|,|Im z|≤|z| and |z|≤|Re z|+|Im z| transfer Cauchyness and convergence. Use lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws for the scalar triangle inequality and multiplicativity; the coordinate inequalities follow by comparing nonnegative squares in the modulus formula. For a supremum-Cauchy sequence x^(m) in c_0, define each coordinate x_j as its unique scalar limit; Apply def-axiom-schema-of-replacement to the uniquely specified ordered pair (j,x_j) for each j; its image is the graph of x. This assembles the coordinate limits without any choice axiom. If ||x^(m)−x^(l)||∞<eta for m,l≥M, passage to each coordinate limit gives |x^(m)_j−x_j|≤eta uniformly in j. In particular x is bounded and ||x^(m)−x||∞≤eta. Given epsilon>0 choose m with this norm <epsilon/2 and then J with |x^(m)_j|<epsilon/2 for j≥J; hence x_j→0. This proves Banach completeness. For P_N, the vector sum is the monoid-valued finite sum of def-linear-combination-and-span; finite support proves the image is in c_0, coordinatewise linearity is explicit, and ||P_Nx||∞≤||x||∞. Since P_Ne_0=e_0 and ||e_0||∞=1, def-operator-norm gives the exact norm 1 after def-bounded-linear-operator supplies the upper bound. The error is sup_{j>N}|x_j|→0. The new theorem applies under AC_omega since the domain is now proved Banach and the displayed estimate is pointwise bounded; it gives the same qualitative boundedness but is not required for the explicit constant. No assertion about general Schauder bases or later basis theorems is made.

references.title: Lin and Rodriguez, MIT 18.102 Complete Lecture Notes

items.title: A complete domain is necessary for sequential uniform boundedness
items.statement: Removing completeness of the domain makes the sequential assertion false, even with explicit operators and no use of choice. Let c_00(K) be the finitely supported sequences indexed by N={0,1,...}, with ||x||∞. Define T_n:c_00(K)→K by T_nx=nx_n for n≥0. Then each T_n is bounded and ||T_n||=n, while for every x the sequence T_nx is eventually zero. The domain is incomplete.
items.strategy: Define c_00 first as the sequences of c_0 that are eventually zero. It is a coordinatewise vector subspace: if x vanishes from M and y from N onward, then ax+by vanishes from M+N onward, using the natural order. Its support is finite because it is a subset of the finite von Neumann natural M; conversely, if a support F is finite, def-countable gives a bijection f:m→F. Prove by induction on the list length m that the range of every f:m→N has a natural upper bound. At m=0 use 0. At m=r+1, apply the induction hypothesis to f restricted to r, obtaining a bound L_r, and use lem-nat-trichotomy to take the larger of L_r and f(r); the only new index is r, which belongs to r+1. Thus F has a natural upper bound L and x_n=0 for n>L. This proves that the eventual-zero definition is exactly finite support, without any choice. The inherited supremum norm is the normed-subspace norm of def-normed-subspace. For K=C, use rem-real-and-complex-normed-space-convention and lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws for the scalar norm, triangle inequality and multiplicativity underlying c_0 and the estimate for T_n; these are choice-free and do not assert scalar completeness. T_n is linear and |T_nx|≤n||x||∞, so def-bounded-linear-operator supplies boundedness; for n≥1 equality is attained at e_n, so def-operator-norm gives ||T_n||=n; T_0=0 has norm 0. The same finite-support bound makes every orbit eventually zero and its initial finite segment bounded. Norms n are unbounded by thm-of-archimedean, whose real-field premise is discharged by cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete. For incompleteness let z^(N)_j=1/(j+1) for j≤N and zero otherwise. For M>N, ||z^(M)−z^(N)||∞=1/(N+2), which tends to zero by cor-archimedean-reciprocal. If z^(N) had a norm limit z in c_00, coordinatewise domination |z_j−z^(N)_j|≤||z−z^(N)||∞ would force z_j=1/(j+1) at each fixed j, contradicting its eventual-zero, equivalently finite-support, property. Thus this is the failure of precisely the Banach-domain hypothesis, with the same zero-based n x_n convention as the design. No assertion about lack of choice follows.
